EXPLAINED 16 September 2026 by J-parity-leftovers-are-a-one-sided-bohr-set. The claim that 26254995 = n_max^par(25781) is the cheapest floor moving the Theorem 4.6 cutoff is confirmed by direct scan -- the first exception moves from 25781 to 50508 there -- and the reason is structural: the surviving lengths are the one-sided Bohr set { L : 0 < g(L) < kappa L } with kappa about 0.63/(n0 ln n0), so raising the floor shrinks the window and the first survivor walks up the record-setters of the one-sided approximation. The next two such floors are 162848325, which moves the cutoff to 101016, and 1044093214, which clears every length below 300000.
